newsitem.title: THAILAND: Investors await Thai Danu, Finance One deal.
newsitem.headline: Investors await Thai Danu, Finance One deal.

text.p: Thai investors are anxiously awaiting word on the outcome of a mega-merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc, a deal that is believed to be in trouble, analysts said on Thursday.

The deal's eventual outcome, which will set the direction for further consolidation in the local finance sector, could become clearer on Friday when the companies are expected to decide the merger's fate in separate board meetings, officials of both firms said.
Both companies had postponed board meetings orginally scheduled for last Friday.
Analysts expect some negative impact on the stock market if either board does not approve the proposed deal. But the damage will be limited, they said.

"There will be some negative impact (on the market). It's quite likely," Andrew Maule, bank analyst at Vickers Ballas, told Reuters. "But I don't think it will be a huge negative impact. At this point, the market has heard several indications the deal is not going well," he added.
Thai Danu is a medium-sized bank while Finance One was formerly the top finance company in the country.
"The deal is very significant. It will be the guideline for other banks and finance companies to integrate in the future," said one analyst at SITCA Investment and Securities.

The proposed deal, which would be the largest between two Thai financial institutions, is believed to have run into trouble in recent weeks because of Finance One's low quality assets and bad debts, analysts said.
"Obviously Thai Danu Bank is concerned about the acquisition of Finance One's assets because they are not sure about the quality (of those assets)," Maule of Vickers Ballas told Reuters.
Finance One has said it has 66 billion baht ($2.54 billion) in outstanding loans -- 20 billion baht of which are in Thailand's troubled property sector.

The Bank of Thailand is lobbying hard to prevent a collapse of the proposed merger because it is a key part of its strategy to strengthen the financial sector by promoting integration among local banks and finance companies.
But Thai Danu officials said the due diligence process had gone too far to make any changes. A memorandum of understanding has already been signed for the proposed merger by the two parties.
Under the original merger terms, announced in late February, Thai Danu had planned to take six billion baht of Finance One's property loans.
Troubles at Finance One led to the revamp of the country's ailing finance sector by the government in March.

Financial institutions, stuck with billions of dollars in sour loans to the depressed property sector, were asked to raise provisions for sub-standard assets while some finance firms were asked to raise capital.
The finance industry is suffering from declining loan portfolio quality, high financing costs and losses due to the depressed stock market, they added.
